text:
anya: Heads-up — product asked for a plan to support org-scoped service account tokens + per-project quotas. Right now API keys are project-first and messy for cross-org apps.

michael: +1. We keep getting support tickets where customers create API keys at org level but the billing/quotas still map to projects.

jamal: Curious — are we talking about a new token type (scoped_token) or layering policies on existing keys?

anya: Proposal in thread: introduce Scoped API Tokens issued to service accounts with explicit scope metadata (org_id, project_ids[], roles[]). Opaque token but a signed JWT for introspection maybe.

sophia: If we use JWTs we can avoid an introspection call for most checks, but then rotation + revocation gets harder. Audit logs also matter.

michael: We should keep tokens revocable immediately. Customers will want to revoke compromised tokens. So either short-lived JWTs + refresh, or opaque token stored server-side (revocation list).

console-ux: From console side — customers want a single flow: create service account -> choose projects -> assign quotas/limits -> generate token. Also show effective rate limits on the token details page.

anya: Right. UX needs to show which project is billed for usage when token hits multiple projects (we have legacy behavior of attributing to default project). That causes confusion.

jamal: Implementation note: our routing layer currently picks model routing by key -> project -> pool. We'll need to change to support token->org->project(s) resolution and fallback rules (e.g., if project_id not in token, deny or route to default with audit).

michael: Quotas: Two models — per-token aggregated across projects, or per-project enforcement. Do customers want per-token cross-project quotas?

sophia: Many customers want both: org-level spend cap, plus per-project SLOs. We should support a hierarchy: token-level, project-level, org-level. Enforcement order: token -> project -> org.

anya: Telemetry: we need new fields in usage events: token_type=scoped, token_owner=service_account_id, allowed_projects=[...], billing_project_resolved. Add audit events for token creation/rotation/revoke.

jamal: Internal API debate: should token validation live in the edge auth proxy (fast path) or in the control-plane service (centralized)? Fast path reduces latency but duplicates revocation state; control-plane centralizes but adds a hop.

michael: My vote: validate minimal claims at edge (org/project present + signature if JWT) and ask control-plane for revocation status asynchronously with cache TTL + webhook to purge. That balances latency and revocation speed.

sophia: For rollout, we need a migration path: 1) opt-in scoped tokens, 2) allow projects to accept both legacy API keys and scoped tokens, 3) deprecate legacy after a long window. Provide a migration CLI that scans usage and suggests mapping.

console-ux: We'll mock the UI in Figma and want feature-flagged rollout by org so sales can enable for enterprise customers first.

auditor-bot: Note: creating org-scoped tokens will require updates to compliance docs and exportable audit trails. Filing ticket DOCS-401.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline check — add feature flag gate + rollout canary set to 5% of orgs.

anya: Action items: (1) jamal + michael to draft schema for scoped token claims + introspection endpoint (2) console-ux to spec UI flows + mockups (3) infra: add auth-proxy cache for revocation + telemetry events (4) product: migration policy + deprecation timeline.

michael: Also add metrics to track "unresolved billing project" events to catch misattribution during migration.

jamal: I'll put up a PR with a minimal prototyping branch for token validation and a wire of the DB migration (service_account_tokens table).

anya: Great — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review. Thanks :thumbsup:

michael: :thumbsup:

sophia: If anyone has edge cases (multi-tenant proxies, proxies that rewrite headers), paste them here before the sync.

jamal: One more — CLI should expose a dry-run mode to show how usage would map after migration. Saves a ton of support tickets.

anya: Yep. Adding that to action item (5).
